manager_or_parent: Externally managed by Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC (Kennedy Lewis Investment Management)
summary: Millrose (NYSE: MRP) is the only land banker that must publish its book. Spun out of Lennar on 2025-02-07 and run for a 1.25%-of-assets fee by Kennedy Lewis, it had $9.25B invested at 2026-09-30 across 156,729 homesites, 834 communities, 30 states and 22 builder counterparties. Lennar is 63.5% of capital at a fixed 8.5% under filed master agreements; the other 21 builders pay a floating 10.8% (floors about 10%, deposits about 10%, 95-96% of capital in cross-termination pools), but only five non-Lennar names are public: New Home Co (Landsea take-private, about $700M), Dream Finders (Beazer takeover, about $1.07B incl. a $488M 12% preferred), Taylor Morrison's Yardly, JPI (multifamily) and Rausch Coleman's seller-side holdback. It has reported no builder walk-aways, forfeitures or renegotiations since inception. Its constraint is capital: debt-to-capitalization 36% against a 33% target after $1.0B of 6.50%/6.75% notes and a new unsecured bank facility, and it will not issue equity below book ($35.24), so growth now comes from takedown recycling, a $250M buyback signals the stock is cheap, and the August 2026 amendments opened rentals. Lennar's founder rights (most-favoured rate, capital priority, pool caps of $50M/$25M at risk per pool) shape what Millrose can offer everyone else.

facts.fact: Walk-away cost for Lennar on a property: it forfeits the 5% up-front payment, owes the unpaid part of the 5% Additional Deposit as a termination fee, must complete the horizontal work in the pool, and loses its options on the other properties in that pool if Millrose cross-terminates.
facts.source_title: Millrose investor presentation, February 2025 (8-K 2025-02-24, Exhibit 99.1), slide 29 (Master Option Agreement)

facts.fact: Deposits under the Lennar Master Option Agreement: (1) an up-front 'Option Payment' (called the Initial Deposit in the 10-K) of 5% of projected total land acquisition and development costs, fully earned when paid; (2) an 'Additional Deposit' of up to 5% of the takedown price of homesites still under option, which Millrose can call as a prepayment on 20 business days' notice when it needs ordinary-course cash flow (credited dollar-for-dollar to takedowns) or which falls due as an Option Termination Payment within 20 business days after Lennar terminates. The two forms of additional deposit together cannot exceed 5%.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Sections 1.6 and 1.9

facts.fact: Lennar's failure to exercise an option or to make a monthly option payment is not a 'default' under the Master Option Agreement: the option simply ends. Millrose's remedies on a builder default are to terminate, keep the option consideration and claim direct damages; it cannot force Lennar to buy and cannot recover consequential or punitive damages.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Sections 1.3 and 17

facts.fact: Cross-termination mechanics (form of Multiparty Cross Agreement): a Cross Termination Event occurs when the option on any pool property ends for a reason other than Millrose's default and Lennar has not bought all its homesites. Millrose then has 20 business days to elect to terminate the options on other properties in that pool, or the right is waived. Each pool's agreement operates independently of the others.
facts.source_title: Form of Multiparty Cross Agreement (8-K Exhibit 10.8), Section 3

facts.fact: Carve-outs from cross-termination: Lennar can cure a single-property default by a bulk purchase where the default cannot be cured by payment and is outside its control; a termination because Lennar bought every homesite does not count; and if Millrose asks Lennar to fee-build the terminated property the event is treated as cured. Where a property is terminated for Lennar's default, remedies are confined to that property.
facts.source_title: Form of Multiparty Cross Agreement (8-K Exhibit 10.8), Section 3(a)-(c)

facts.fact: Pool sizing rule: Lennar's 'Total Payment Obligation' per pool (all 5% option payments plus all additional deposits made or owed for properties in the pool) may never exceed $50 million for pools of seed properties or $25 million for pools of future properties. Lennar proposes the pools, Millrose's approval cannot be unreasonably withheld, 'primary consideration' goes to diversity by geography, community and home type, and pools must be structured to stay off Lennar's balance sheet.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Section 2(a)

facts.fact: Inferred from the pool caps: with up to 10% of cost at stake per property (5% up front plus up to 5% additional), a $50 million cap implies a seed pool of roughly $500 million of takedown value and a $25 million cap a future pool of roughly $250 million. That is the most Lennar loses by abandoning an entire pool. Calculation: cap / 10%.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Section 2(a)

facts.fact: Takedown flexibility for Lennar: up to four quarterly extensions of a takedown on five business days' notice with no extension fee stated (it must be caught up by the final takedown); it may accelerate takedowns up to 50% of a pool's homesites, and a bulk purchase above 50% requires buying every homesite in the pool.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Section 1.4

facts.fact: Pause periods in the option agreement: up to two pauses of up to six months each per property, triggered by a seasonally adjusted home-price decline of 10% or more in the MSA on the Burns index (measured from the deal's effective date) or a pandemic / public health emergency; two more six-month pauses with Millrose's approval, not to be unreasonably withheld, if the condition persists. During a pause takedown and construction deadlines extend, no closings happen and the fee runs at the Pause Rate, 50% of the Applicable Rate.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Section 1.4(e)

facts.fact: Lennar can also call pauses at its sole discretion under the Founder's Rights Agreement (still capped at two per community in total, six months each, at half rate), but while any Lennar property is in such a pause Lennar loses its most-favoured-rate right on new deals.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Section 3.07

facts.fact: Carry costs sit with the builder: Lennar pays real estate taxes, assessments, HOA dues, utilities, maintenance and insurance on optioned property through the option termination date, plus closing costs and transfer taxes at takedown.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Sections 1.8, 6 and 8

facts.fact: After a termination Lennar has no right of first offer or refusal on the retained land. It has 90 days to buy homesites where it has started vertical construction, otherwise it must remove the construction on request. Millrose may within 20 days ask Lennar to act as fee builder on the land, which Lennar must do only where it is active in that market, for a management fee of 20% of reimbursable costs plus overhead and sales fees, paid by Millrose.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Section 2(d) and Exhibit E (form of Fee Builder Agreement)

facts.fact: Program has no end date and no volume commitment from Lennar: the acquisition period runs until both sides agree in writing to stop admitting properties; Lennar need not offer deals and grants no exclusivity, first look or right of first refusal. The obligation runs the other way: while Lennar has capital reserved, Millrose must on Lennar's request acquire every proposed project that meets the Program Criteria, signing documents within 15 business days.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Sections 2(b), 4(a), 4(c), 4(e)

facts.fact: Program Criteria (the Lennar buy-box): all material discretionary approvals obtained (entitled land only); primary use single-family detached or attached homesites; no building moratorium; a Phase I environmental report dated within 180 days of closing; a full takedown schedule; Lennar responsible for finished-homesite costs above the contract sum; and Millrose need not buy if more than 40% of total committed capital would sit in a single state.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Exhibit F

facts.fact: Development funding: Millrose funds horizontal development up to the budgeted contract sum under the Master Construction Agreement; Lennar performs the work as contractor and is solely responsible for cost overruns unless an independent consultant determines otherwise; home construction is outside the funded work. Lennar Corporation backs this with an unlimited parent Payment and Performance Guaranty covering the program, option and construction agreements.
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2025-02-07 (spin-off completion), Item 1.01

facts.fact: Founder's Rights Agreement (2025-02-07; Millrose with U.S. Home, Lennar Homes Holding and CalAtlantic) gives Lennar eight rights: management succession consent, equity price protection, capital priority, enforcement, rate adjustment, the debt-to-equity limit, secured-financing collateral consent, and pause designation. Millrose may not grant these rights to anyone else without Lennar's consent. Most last until Lennar-contributed cash and capital assets fall below 10% of Millrose's total GAAP assets for six consecutive months.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Articles II-III

facts.fact: Capital Priority Right: from 2026-03-01 and every three months after, Lennar may reserve Millrose capital for its own deals for the next three-month period; what it does not reserve is lost ('use it or lose it'), though lost amounts not committed to third parties are restored at the next date. The reservable pool is Lennar's initial capital (the value of the contributed assets, about $5.2 billion of land book value plus cash per the recitals) and recycled capital, plus 25% of new non-revolver debt and 25% of new equity that Millrose raises beyond the first $2 billion, capped at $10 billion less the initial capital. If Millrose cannot fund a committed Lennar deal it owes Lennar's damages including replacement financing cost.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Section 3.03

facts.fact: Enforcement Rights: if Millrose fails to convey a homesite within 10 days after notice, Lennar gets specific performance without bond, pre-agreed confession of judgment and attorney-in-fact powers, and may stop monthly option payments across all programs until cured. If Millrose disputes in good faith on a pooling-violation claim Lennar keeps paying, and the loser of the dispute pays the other three times the monthly option payments made during the dispute period.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Article IV

facts.fact: Equity price protection: if within 18 months of 2025-02-07 another customer receives Millrose equity for future property assets worth more than $500 million at a per-share price below Lennar's effective price, Millrose must issue extra Class A shares at no cost so that the original spin shares are re-priced to the lower level (the new customer does not participate).
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Section 3.02

facts.fact: Lennar consent is required to replace the manager (not to be unreasonably withheld; 10 business days to object) and to approve successors to the named key men, David K. Chene and Darren L. Richman. Lennar's consent, in its sole discretion, is also needed before any Lennar-optioned property is pledged in a financing alongside property optioned to another customer.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Sections 3.01 and 3.06

facts.fact: Recognition, Subordination and Non-Disturbance Agreement (2025-02-07): Lennar subordinates its option rights to Millrose's intercompany mortgages and pledge; Millrose must give 10 business days' notice before foreclosing and Lennar may buy the note for the amount owed.
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2025-02-07 (spin-off completion), Item 1.01

facts.fact: HOPP'R ('Homesite Option Purchase Platform') is Lennar's, not Millrose's: Lennar-Millrose HOPP'R, LLC sublicenses the rights to Millrose Holdings on a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, non-transferable basis for internal use, perpetual subject to limited termination conditions. Lennar may license the same platform to other land banks.
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2025-02-07 (spin-off completion), Item 1.01 (Sublicense Agreement)

facts.fact: Management Agreement (2025-02-07): the manager is Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Kennedy Lewis Investment Management. Fee is 1.25% per annum of Tangible Assets (0.3125% a quarter), paid quarterly in advance on 1 January, April, July and October, and payable regardless of performance. Through about the first 12 months the base is total assets including cash, less intangibles and non-revenue-generating assets; after that cash is excluded.
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Sections 1 and 10

facts.fact: There is no incentive fee, carried interest or equity grant to the manager in the Management Agreement. Out of the 1.25% the manager pays all company operating expenses, including officers and directors' cash fees up to $1.25 million a year (growing 3% a year). Millrose reimburses only offering costs, extraordinary litigation and M&A costs, and the cost of owning and maintaining land where a builder failed to exercise its option.
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Sections 1 and 11

facts.fact: Manager term and exit: three-year initial term to 2028-02-07, then automatic one-year renewals. Millrose can end it without cause only on 180 days' notice, with a two-thirds vote of independent directors during the initial term (majority at a term end), on grounds of materially detrimental performance or an excessive fee. Termination for cause (uncured material breach, insolvency, fraud or gross negligence, dissolution) takes a majority of independent directors, 30 days' notice and no fee.
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Sections 14-15

facts.fact: Manager termination fee: 3.0x the average annual management fee if average annual return on equity over the prior three years is 7% or more; otherwise 2.5x if terminated before the initial term ends and 1.5x at or after expiry. The average uses the two years before termination (annualised if shorter).
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Section 1 (Termination Fee)

facts.fact: 2025-09-08 pricing / 2025-09-11 closing: second bond, $750M of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due 2032-09-15, priced at par and upsized by $250M from the $500M launch size, 12.5 bps tighter than the 2030 notes five weeks earlier for two more years of tenor. Proceeds triggered mandatory prepayment of the DDTL, which was repaid in full and terminated on 2025-09-11. Net proceeds $737.5M per the FY2025 10-K.

facts.fact: Fitch actions: expected rating assigned 2025-08-04 and final 'BBB-' assigned 2025-08-12 to the $1.25B 6.375% notes due 2030, equalized with the long-term issuer rating, Stable outlook; 'BBB-(EXP)' assigned 2025-09-09 to the 2032 notes. Fitch's stated downgrade triggers: Fitch-calculated leverage (gross debt / tangible equity) sustained above 0.75x, unsecured debt below 35% of total debt, failure to add third-party builders, or a material decline in builder credit quality. Upgrade would need leverage sustained below 0.5x and is 'not expected near term'. Constraints cited: concentrated builder relationships, short standalone history, REIT payout limiting retained capital.
facts.source_title: Fitch Ratings release republished by MarketScreener, 2025-08-12 (and 2025-09-09 release)

facts.fact: 2025-08-04 pricing / 2025-08-07 closing: first bond, $1.25B of 6.375% senior unsecured notes due 2030-08-01, priced at par and upsized by $250M from the $1.0B launch size. FY2025 10-K gives net proceeds of $1,227.9M (about 1.8% all-in issuance cost, my calculation from $1,250.0M gross).
